newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zedillo says forex "adjustments" good for Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Zedillo says forex "adjustments" good for Mexico.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said on Friday that "natural adjustments" in the foreign exchange and financial markets have not hindered economic recovery in Mexico.

"Indeed, flexibility in financial variables, that is, the freedom for them to adjust to market forces, is the best antidote and way to avoid situations which in the recent past caused a great harm to the country," Zedillo said in the wake of instability for the Mexican peso this week.
Zedillo said the lack of severe repercussions from unsteady financial markets was due to the consistency and flexibility of the economic program pursued by his administration.

"Today, our short-term obligations, which used to put disproportionate pressure on our economy, have been settled by substantially improving conditions of payment on our foreign debt," Zedillo said in a speech to honorary consuls to Mexico.
Mexico's short-term debt maturities totaled $41 billion in 1995, he said, in addition to a current account deficit of $30 billion that Mexico had run up in 1994.
